finding: The selected retention requirement starts the 30-day period at the successful tracked commit and limits it to successful promotions. ADR 0005 and rules/02 establish only the 30-day duration for promotion artifact retention. Neither supplies a start event, a freshness boundary, or a success-only scope. The point from which the applicable duration runs is therefore unknown in the complete request, so the retention obligation cannot be shown to be satisfiable as written.

The Design Rationale justifies only per-read policy evaluation. It gives no alternatives, accepted costs, or rejection reasons for the important choice that authorization depends only on operation and is identical for every verified principal, with no resource scope. This non-obvious choice is unexplained, so its trade-off for principals and resources cannot be assessed.

The ADR Evaluation treats the new rollback recovery result as an expression of the existing ADR 0001 rollback responsibility and concludes that no new ADR is needed. ADR 0001 states that it does not define the recovery-result fields and failure lifecycle introduced by this change, and architecture/02 says the same. The new public recovery result and its failure lifecycle therefore have no ADR evaluation. promotion-runtime defers that evaluation to this design, so no document performs it.

The Security Boundary conclusion says the design creates no new durable security decision because it does not move identity, policy, credential, or persistent state. The same design adds a protected access review (line 5) and places the authorization decision in the Access Review Module (line 27). Authorization is decided only by operation for every verified principal, and the caller-supplied resourceId becomes the read source. That authorization model is a security boundary decision, and the ADR Evaluation neither inventories nor justifies it, so the no-ADR conclusion is unsupported.

The Module Design section uses Not required, but the change adds a new caller-visible summary field to the public promote(inputPath) successful result. That result is part of the promotion Module Interface (promotion-runtime Successful Result). Changing an Interface is outside the Not required condition, so the complete Module Design format applies. The stated reason that the existing result owner serializes the field does not address the Interface change.

The Not required paragraph says only that the optimization 'preserves the current architecture'. That restates the conclusion. It does not explain why the Module responsibility, Interface, Seam, dependency direction, authority, and data flow stay unchanged when repeated per-field scanning is replaced by a single forward cursor pass. The reasoning is generic and circular, so the exemption is not supported.

Artifact validation has more than one responsible owner. Promotion validates the immutable artifact before any persistence write (line 11). Readiness also validates it before promotion, and Promotion validates request and artifact again before the persistence preconditions (line 27). The design does not name a single owner for this behavior or justify the second validation, so the duplicated responsibility is not resolved.

Readiness must confirm artifact.requestId against an immutable request and inputPath against the path bound to the current request, but no caller-visible result is defined for a mismatch. The public promote(inputPath) Interface carries no request, and no supplied Input defines the immutable request or how the path is bound to it. The Failure Results list covers only missing, non-string, or empty inputPath, so the precondition cannot be implemented or its failure observed.

Testing Decisions exclude request binding and retentionDays application from public lifecycle tests and verify them only by source review. ADR 0004 requires runtime behavior to be tested through the public lifecycle Interface. Retention application determines what persistence receives and retains, so it is runtime behavior, and the required public test boundary for it and for request binding is missing.

The rollback failure shape is {recovered: false, failureCode, priorTrackedState, baselineStatus} and has a single failureCode. Line 35 says the Recovery Module keeps the original commit failure, and line 59 says the restore failure is also kept while forming this shape. The Interface never states whether failureCode is the original commitFailureCode or the restore failure code, so the caller-visible failure value is undefined.

Testing Decisions cover only successful rollback and invalid-input first error. The rollback failure result, including its baselineStatus of removed or retained, has no public lifecycle test boundary, even though the Interface defines it. The scenario that produces it (a failed restore) is not named as a public test case.

renderReport(source) returns invalid-input only when source is missing. The architecture's analogous invalid-input contract for inputPath covers missing, non-string, and empty values. The Interface leaves non-string and empty source undefined, so the caller-visible result for those inputs is not specified.

The design says access review trusts the verified principal passed by the caller boundary and decides for that principal, but the reviewAccess(request) Interface accepts only the immutable request. The verified principal is not an input of the Interface, and no result is defined for a missing or invalid principal. The Testing Decisions require checking that the principal comes from the caller boundary, which the Interface cannot express.

Testing Decisions require a Policy Adapter failure case, but the Seam and Other Results define only allowed, denied, invalid-policy, and invalid-request outcomes. The observable result of a Policy Adapter failure is not defined, so the required public test boundary has no contract to verify against.

Authorization is decided only by operation, and the caller-supplied resourceId, which needs only to be a non-empty string, becomes the source for readArtifact after an allowed operation. Nothing in the Interface requires resourceId to name an authorized canonical artifact, and the Production Adapter reads from any caller source. An allowed operation can therefore read a resource that the policy never approved, and the invariant that reads occur only for authorized resources is missing.

renderReport and parseArtifact each implement the same Invalid Artifact Contract validation, as line 90 accepts, instead of sharing one validation policy. This duplicates runtime domain policy across two operations, so a change to the artifact contract must be made in two places. The stated reason rests on the Parser size limit, but architecture/05 limits input-too-large to the Current Parser Contract, so the size limit is not part of the shared validation contract.

The Dependencies and Data Flow section of this complete-format spec contains no Source/Authority table. The authorities it declares (the existing tracked state as the current authoritative result, the temporary baseline as recovery evidence only, the artifact supplied by Readiness, and the failed-attempt identity and failure code) appear only in prose. rules/05 requires one Source/Authority table listing every declared authority in this section.

The 30-day retention obligation has no defined durable state or owner after the tracked commit. persist accepts retentionDays and 'consumes' it, but the design does not say what is stored or where. Line 15 excludes later removal from this operation. Line 89 and ADR 0005 limit Readiness to applying the policy and bar other Modules from creating or changing durable retention authority, so no permitted owner is assigned for the durable retention state.
